verdict: Deere grew revenue 5% to $12.6B and lifted profit to $1.4B as construction and small-farm equipment strength outweighed a still-soft market for its biggest farm machines.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +5% YoY — net sales and revenues of $12,608M

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $4.75 a year ago, on net income attributable to Deere of $1,379M

kpis.label: Construction & Forestry sales
kpis.note: +18% YoY, with operating profit up 84% to $436M

kpis.label: Full-year guidance
kpis.note: Net income attributable to Deere expected for fiscal 2026 — guidance was raised with this report

segments.name: Production and Precision Agriculture
segments.note: The biggest farm machines — large tractors, combines and planters — plus precision-ag technology. Net sales fell 6% on lower shipment volumes, partly offset by higher prices. Operating profit was $527M, a 13.2% margin.

segments.name: Small Agriculture and Turf
segments.note: Smaller tractors, lawn and turf equipment. Net sales rose 12% on higher volumes and prices. Operating profit jumped 28% to $622M, an 18.4% margin — the most profitable equipment business this quarter.

segments.name: Construction and Forestry
segments.note: Construction, roadbuilding and forestry machines. Net sales rose 18% on higher volumes and prices, and operating profit almost doubled to $436M, a 12.1% margin.

segments.name: Finance and interest income
segments.note: Interest and fees earned on loans and leases that finance equipment purchases — mostly from the Financial Services business ($1,253M of it on an external basis), which earned net income of $219M in the quarter.

segments.name: Other income
segments.note: Miscellaneous revenue outside equipment sales and financing, as reported on the face of the income statement.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing new machines and precision-agriculture technology — guidance systems, automation and software. About flat vs a year ago.

opex.name: Selling, administrative and general
opex.note: The dealer network, marketing and the back office. About flat vs a year ago, so sales growth dropped through to profit.

opex.name: Other operating expenses
opex.note: Mostly the running costs of the Financial Services loan and lease book that are not interest — credit costs and lease expenses, net of related items.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $710M, shown as other expense. Most of it — $661M inside Financial Services — is the cost of borrowing the money that Deere then lends to farmers and dealers to buy equipment, so it works like a cost of the loan book rather than ordinary corporate debt interest. The flow also adds $24M of equity income from part-owned affiliates, shown as its own line in the chart math.

takeaways.title: Growth came from the smaller machines
takeaways.text: Total net sales and revenues rose 5% to $12,608M. Small Agriculture & Turf grew 12% to $3,383M and Construction & Forestry grew 18% to $3,618M, more than covering a 6% fall in Production & Precision Agriculture — the biggest farm machines — to $3,998M as farmers held back in a soft large-ag market.

takeaways.title: Profit rose even at the cycle's low point
takeaways.text: Net income was $1,377M in total, $1,379M of it attributable to Deere shareholders (outside partners in some subsidiaries lost $2M), or $5.10 per share vs $4.75 a year ago. Deere calls 2026 the bottom of the farm-equipment cycle and raised full-year net income guidance to $4.75B–$5.00B.

takeaways.title: A tariff recovery flattered production costs
takeaways.text: The quarter includes $110M of tariff recoveries ($382M so far this year) booked mainly against production costs. Leaving that one-off benefit aside, margins were helped by higher prices and volumes in two of the three equipment businesses, partly offset by higher production costs.

oneTimers: Deere recorded $110M of tariff recoveries in the quarter ($382M in the first nine months of fiscal 2026), mainly credited against production costs. It is a refund-style benefit, not normal selling profit, so this quarter's margins look a little better than the underlying run rate.
footerNote: Deere reports no operating-income line; this chart adapts it — interest is shown as other expense, equity income below operating profit.
follow100Note: All figures as reported, in $M: cost of revenue is cost of sales ($7,939M); operating expenses are research and development, selling/administrative/general, and other operating expenses; interest expense ($710M) is shown as other expense and equity income ($24M) below operating profit — revenues $12,608M less total costs $10,726M equals pre-tax income of $1,882M, and $1,882M less $529M of tax plus $24M of equity income equals total net income of $1,377M. Of that, $1,379M was attributable to Deere & Company because noncontrolling interests recorded a $2M loss.
